papers.title: Development of a Cherenkov Telescope for the Detection of Ultra-High Energy Neutrinos with EUSO-SPB2 and POEMMA
authors: Lawrence Rudnick Harvard-Smithsonian Center for Astrophysics
T. U. O. A. I. Huntsville
papers.abstract: The detection of astrophysical neutrinos by IceCube and the potential to constrain source models of ultra-high energy cosmic rays provide the motivation to develop instruments for the observation of neutrinos above $10^7$ GeV. Among the different techniques to detect ultra-high energy neutrinos is the Earth-skimming technique. It makes use of the fact that the tau produced in a tau neutrino interaction inside the Earth can emerge from the ground and initiate an upward-going particle shower in the atmosphere. The particle shower and thus the neutrino can be reconstructed by measuring the Cherenkov and radio emission from the shower particles. In this presentation, we discuss our ongoing development of a Cherenkov telescope for the detection of tau neutrinos, which is to be deployed on the Extreme Universe Space Observatory Super Pressure Balloon 2 (EUSO-SPB2) and is a precursor experiment for the proposed Probe of Extreme Multi-Messenger Astrophysics (POEMMA) mission. POEMMA aims at the detection of ultrahigh energy cosmic rays and ultrahigh energy neutrinos from low earth orbit. The 1 m$^2$ Cherenkov telescope for EUSO-SPB2 will use silicon photomultipliers coupled to a 100 MS/s readout based on the ASIC for General Electronics for TPC`s (AGET) switch capacitor ring sampler. We present the optics, results from our studies to qualify the readout concept and the design of the mechanical integration of the photon detectors and the readout into the telescope.

papers.title: From Idea to Implementation: Evaluating the Influence of Large Language Models in Software Development - An Opinion Paper
authors: Niamh St John Lynch . Nikhil Singh
The Centre for Research in Engineering Surface Technol Dublin
papers.abstract: The introduction of transformer architecture was a turning point in Natural Language Processing (NLP). Models based on the transformer architecture such as Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformers (BERT) and Generative Pre-Trained Transformer (GPT) have gained widespread popularity in various applications such as software development and education. The availability of Large Language Models (LLMs) such as ChatGPT and Bard to the general public has showcased the tremendous potential of these models and encouraged their integration into various domains such as software development for tasks such as code generation, debugging, and documentation generation. In this study, opinions from 11 experts regarding their experience with LLMs for software development have been gathered and analysed to draw insights that can guide successful and responsible integration. The overall opinion of the experts is positive, with the experts identifying advantages such as increase in productivity and reduced coding time. Potential concerns and challenges such as risk of over-dependence and ethical considerations have also been highlighted.

papers.abstract: Abstract We present the Evolutionary Map of the Universe (EMU) survey conducted with the Australian Square Kilometre Array Pathfinder (ASKAP). EMU aims to deliver the touchstone radio atlas of the southern hemisphere. We introduce EMU and review its science drivers and key science goals, updated and tailored to the current ASKAP five-year survey plan. The development of the survey strategy and planned sky coverage is presented, along with the operational aspects of the survey and associated data analysis, together with a selection of diagnostics demonstrating the imaging quality and data characteristics. We give a general description of the value-added data pipeline and data products before concluding with a discussion of links to other surveys and projects and an outline of EMU’s legacy value.

question: What are the key technological, narrative, and market trends shaping the current development of galgames?
hypothesis: Galgames incorporating AI-driven procedural narrative generation achieve higher player retention rates than those using linear, pre-scripted storylines.
methodology: Design a short galgame with two versions: an AI-driven procedural narrative branch using a language model (e.g., GPT) to generate dynamic dialogues and plot, and a linear, pre-scripted story with fixed choices. Recruit 30–50 student participants from campus, randomly assign each to play one version. Track in-game metrics (playtime, replays, completion rate) as retention indicators, and collect post-play survey data on engagement and narrative satisfaction. Compare retention metrics between groups using independent t-tests; analyze survey responses thematically to evaluate if AI-driven narratives yield higher retention and perceived quality.
proposal: Despite the popularity of galgames (visual novels with a focus on romance and interactive storytelling), the academic literature lacks investigation into their current development trends, with existing studies addressing unrelated topics such as neutrino detection and software development tools. This gap prompts the research question: What are the key technological, narrative, and market trends shaping the modern development of galgames? We hypothesize that galgames incorporating AI-driven procedural narrative generation achieve higher player retention rates than those using linear, pre-scripted storylines. To test this, we will develop a short galgame with two versions—one using a language model (e.g., GPT) for dynamic dialogue and plot generation, and another with a fixed, branching narrative—and recruit 30–50 student participants to play one version each, tracking in-game retention metrics (playtime, replays, completion rate) and administering post-play surveys on engagement and satisfaction. Data analysis will employ independent t-tests for retention metrics and thematic analysis for survey responses. The expected contribution is empirical evidence on the efficacy of AI-driven narrative generation in galgames, offering actionable insights for developers and advancing game studies research on interactive storytelling.

evaluation.comments: The proposal is clearly written and logically structured, with a feasible methodology. However, it is not grounded in the retrieved papers, which are entirely unrelated to galgame development; thus, literature alignment is minimal.

baseline.proposal: This proposal outlines a multidisciplinary approach to understanding and advancing trends in galgame development. By leveraging large language models (Paper 2) for automated narrative generation, employing radio survey techniques (Paper 3) to map genre evolution, utilizing neutrino detection optics (Paper 1) for innovative visual effects, and adopting the cooperative funding model of the BRICS bank (Paper 4), we aim to create a comprehensive framework that accelerates galgame production and diversifies its thematic and technical landscape.
